PARTI
PRELIMINARY PROVISIONS

Citation and Commencement
1. (1) These Regulations may be cited as the Environment Assessment Regulations, 2022.

(2) This Notice shall come into force on the date of publication in the Gazette.

 
Application

2. These Regulations shall apply to the Government and any other persons, bodies and
institutions.

Interpretation
3. In these Regulations, unless the context otherwise requires —
“Act” means the Environment Management Act 2002;

“alternatives” in relation to a proposed activity, means different means of meeting the general
purpose and requirements of the activity, which may include alternatives to -

(a) the property on which or location where it is proposed to undertake the activity;
(b) the type of activity to be undertaken;

(c) the design or layout of the activity;

(d) the technology to be used in the activity; and

(e) the operational aspects of thie activity;

“affected party” means any person whose life, health, wellbeing, quality of life and livelihood may
be affected directly or indirectly by a proposed project, policy, plan or programme;

“Authority” means the Eswatini Environment Authority;

“authorization letter’ means an approval issued by the Authority under these Regulations which
certifies that the Authority has consented to an existing undertaking continuing to operate, or, to a
proposed project proceeding, subject to the project proponent or a project proponent of an existing
undertaking complying with the conditions specified in the approval and in the approved
comprehensive mitigation plan;

“category” means a class or projects to which a proposed project may be assigned under
sub-regulation 11(1) and which is subject to a specific environmental review procedure;

“comprehensive mitigation plan” means a document containing a description of the mitigation
measures to be implemented that would prevent, reduce or otherwise manage the environmental
impacts of a project and which are done according to the reporting requirements in the Second
Schedule;

“cumulative environmental impacts” means the effects resulting from the sum of interaction of
impacts, generated by one or more than one undertaking, for a certain period of time.

“environmental audit” means work done to identify and evaluate the environmental impacts of
existing projects which is done according to the reporting requirements in the Third Schedule;

“environmental impact” means any positive or negative impact, on the environment, on any form
of life, on the social, economic or cultural conditions that influence human life, or on any
inter-relationship between these elements or factors, which is, will be, or may be, directly or indi-
rectly caused by an existing or proposed project, policy, plan or programme;

“environmental assessment” means the process for the orderly and systematic identification,
prediction and evaluation of -

 
$4

(a) the likely environmental, socio-economic, cultural and health effects of a proposed project
or an existing undertaking: and

(b) the mitigation and management of those effects,

which process extends from the initial concept of the proposal through implementation to completion,
and where appropriate, decommissioning;

“environmental compliance certificate” means a certificate issued by the Authority under these
Regulations which certifies that a project proponent or a project proponent of an existing undertaking,
has upon completion of project activities or upon undertaking an environmental audit, complied with
the conditions specified in the authorization letter and in the approved Comprehensive Mitigation
Plan;

“environment evaluation report” means an initial report which a project proponent is required to
prepare and submit prior to commencement of a project:

“environmental impact” includes any direct or indirect, positive or negative change in the environment
caused by man-made works or activity when such change affects life in general, biodiversity, the
quality or a significant quantity of natural or environmental resources and their use, wellbeing,
health, personal safety, habits and customs, the cultural heritage or legitimate means of livelihood;

“environmental management plan” means a plan prepared under regulation 12 (2) that describes
how activities that may have significant impact on the environment may be controlled, monitored
and mitigated;

“environmentally sensitive area” means an area which merits a high degree of environmental
protection because the environment in that area, or any constituent part of it, is rare, endangered, or
sensitive to harm, or has particular environmental, archaeological, social, or cultural significance or
value, whether or not the area is legally or administratively protected, and includes areas designated
as environmentally sensitive by the Minister;

“Environmental Assessment Practitioner” means a person qualified and accredited to undertake
environmental assessment in accordance with regulations 8 and 9;

“existing undertaking” means an enterprise or activity which has been implemented whether with or
without authorization or environmental clearance certificate issued under these Regulations or The
Environmental Audit, Assessment and Review Regulations, 2000;

“initial environmental evaluation” means an environmental analysis of a proposed project whose
environmental impacts may be easily determined and for which there are appropriate, well known
and tested mitigation measures;

“interested party” is any natural or legal person who has an interest in the impact of a project, plan,
policy or programme on the environment;

“mitigation” means, in respect of a proposed or existing undertaking, the elimination, reduction or
control of the adverse environmental effects of the undertaking, and includes restitution for any
damage to the environment caused by such effects through replacement, restoration, compensation
or any other means;

“prescribed fee” means the fees prescribed in the Eighth Schedule;
“project brief” means a document which incorporates a brief plan or outline proposal for a project

which contains sufficient information to enable the Authority to determine to which category the
proposed project should be assigned; and

 
SS

“project proponent” means a person responsible for initiating a project and obtaining the appropriate
authorization.

PART IL
INSTITUTIONAL FRAMEWORK FOR ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

Functions of Authority

4. (1) The Authority shall have the overall responsibility for regulating and managing

environmental assessment in Eswatini in accordance with the provisions of the Act.
(2) The Authority shall —
(a) facilitate the environmental assessment process;

(b) undertake project screening and issue Authorization Letters or record of decision and
Environmental Compliance Certificates;

(c) ensure compliance with environmental assessment provisions in terms of the Act;

(d) manage the production and update guidelines on environmental assessment practice
and procedures;

(e) assist line ministries or agencies in the preparation of sector-specific guidelines on
environmental assessment practice and procedures;

(f) maintain and update a register of accredited Environmental Assessment Practitioners
annually;

=

support and encourage the work of national and international organizations involved in
environmental assessment and standards;

(g

(h) maintain a data base of all projects and existing undertakings which have undergone or
undergoing environmental assessment;

(i) maintain a central library of environmental assessment and audit reports; and

(j) perform roles and responsibilities that are necessary for carrying out the objectives of
these Regulations and the Act.

Role of Ministries, Government Departments and Public Agencies

5. The Authority may enter into memoranda of understanding or agreement with such public
institutions, ministries or government departments as the Authority may deem necessary and may
in accordance with such memoranda of understanding or agreement delegate any of its functions or
responsibilities for carrying out the objectives of these Regulations and the Act.

Appointment Panel of Experts
6. (1) The Authority may from time to time appoint such number of persons with such expertise
in environmental assessment, to the Panel of Experts as the Authority may deem necessary

to assist the Authority in undertaking review of environmental assessments.

(2) The Panel of experts appointed under sub-regulation (1) shall serve in their professional
capacity and shall advise the Authority based on the terms of reference for each task.

 
S6

(3) Any person who has an interest, direct or indirect, in any review of an environmental
assessment shall not be eligible for appointment to the Panel of Experts.

(4) Members of the Panel shall be paid such fees or allowances on such terms and
conditions, as may be commensurate with the nature and scope of the task, to be
determined by the Board.

Confidentiality

7. Unless otherwise allowed or required by these Regulations, a person who is a staff member of the
Authority or a person who is appointed to the Panel of experts shall not, without a written consent of
the Director, publish or disclose to any third party other than in the course of duty, the contents of any
document, communication, or information which relates to the business of the Authority and which
has come to the knowledge of that person or expert in the course of their duty under this Act.

Duties of Project Proponents
8. The project proponent shall -
(a) prepare project briefs, as required under the Act and these Regulations;

(b) engage an Environmental Assessment Practitioner for purposes of undertaking
environmental assessment or audit and shall bear the cost of such engagement;

(c) ensure that every service provider engaged by the project proponent in relation to the
project or existing undertaking complies with all the terms and conditions stipulated in the
authorization letter or environmental compliance certificate;

(d) provide the Environmental Assessment Practitioner with access to information at the
disposal of the project proponent regarding the application, whether or not the information
is favourable to the project proponent; and

(e) ensure that the environmental assessment procedures specified in the Act, these regulations
and guidelines are followed.

Environmental Assessment Practitioners
9. (1) A person shall not undertake environmental assessment under these Regulations and the
Act unless that person is registered as an Environmental Assessment Practitioner by an accreditation

body recognized in Eswatini.

(2) The Authority shall keep a copy of the register of accredited Environmental Assessment
Practitioners.

(3) An Environmental Assessment Practitioner shall undertake responsibilities professionally and

objectively as required by law and shall comply with the Environmental Assessment Practitioners
Code of Conduct provided in the First Schedule.

PART III
EXISTING PROJECTS AND PROPOSED PROJECTS

Environmental Audit Reports

10. (1) The Authority shall identify, through inspections and monitoring, existing undertakings
which cause concern to the Authority or to the public because of their impact on the environment.

 
S7

(2) The project proponent of an identified existing undertaking shall submit an environment
assessment report and a comprehensive mitigation plan to the Authority within six (6) months after
notification to do so.

(3) A project proponent on whom a notice to submit an environment assessment report and
comprehensive mitigation plan is served under sub-regulation 1 shall -

(a) submit the environment assessment report and comprehensive mitigation plan together
with the prescribed fee to the Authority within six (6) months of the date of the notice;

(b) indicate any information in the environment assessment report and the comprehensive
mitigation plan which the project proponent considers should not be made public on
the basis that it is commercially confidential or that disclosure would be contrary to the
public interest and shall indicate the grounds for maintaining the confidentiality of the
information; and

(c) bear the costs of the preparing the environment assessment report and the
comprehensive mitigation plan.

(4) The Authority shall consider any environment assessment report and comprehensive

mitigation plan submitted to it and shall -

(a) issue a notice of acceptance to the project proponent if the Authority considers that the
environment assessment report and the comprehensive mitigation plan—

(i) comply with the requirements of these Regulations and any relevant guidelines
published by the Authority; and

(ii) are satisfactory to enable a decision to be made as to whether or not the
Authority should issue an authorization letter, and if so, to determine the terms
and conditions on which it should be issued; or

(b) notify the project proponent of the amendments to the environment assessment report
or the comprehensive mitigation plan which the Authority requires and the date by
which the amended document has to be resubmitted to the Authority together with the
prescribed fee; and

(c) where the Authority is satisfied that some of the information in the environment
assessment report or the comprehensive mitigation plan should not be made public on
the grounds of commercial confidentiality or in the public interest, the Authority shall,
by notice in writing, require the project proponent to submit a summary of that
environment assessment report or the comprehensive mitigation plan which excludes
the confidential information, within ten (10) days of the notice.

(5) Where the Authority is not satisfied that a summary which has been submitted in response to
a notice under sub-regulation (3) (c), is sufficiently clear, comprehensive or accurate to enable the
public to appreciate the full environmental implications of the undertaking bearing in mind the need
to maintain the confidentiality of certain information, the Authority shall require the project
proponent to submit a revised summary within a period specified by the Authority.

(6) The Authority may distribute copies of the environment assessment report and the comprehensive
mitigation plan to every Ministry concerned or responsible for the control of the project for its
comments.

(7) A ministry required under sub-regulation (5) to comment on an environment assessment report
or a comprehensive mitigation plan shall submit its comments to the Authority within a period of ten
(10) days after receipt of the copies of the environment assessment report and the comprehensive

 
S8
mitigation plan.

(8) An environment assessment report, comprehensive mitigation plan or summary of one of
these documents, in respect of which the Authority has issued a notice of acceptance, shall be a
public document and may be inspected by the public at a place designated by the Authority and may
be copied at a specified fee.

(9) The Authority may make availiable copies of an environment assessment report and the
comprehensive mitigation plan or any summary of these documents for inspection by members of
the public at selected locations in the vicinity of a project, to which it relates, for a period of not
less than fifteen (15) days.

(10) The procedure for public review, inspection, submission of comments and objections to a
proposed project shall be in accordance with regulation 17.

Submission of Project Briefs

11. (1) The project proponent of a proposed project which requires a permit, license, approval or
other consent under any written law shall submit a project brief which incorporates a brief plan or

outline proposal for the project and which contains sufficient information to enable the Authority to

determine to which category the proposed project should be assigned in accordance with regulation
ll.

(2) A project brief shall contain -
(a) the site description of the environment;
(b) the objectives and nature of the project;

(c) the summary of the main activities that will be undertaken during site preparation and
construction and after the development is operational;

(d) the raw and other materials that will be used in the project;
(e) the products and by-products of the project; and

(f) the expected socio-economic impacts of the project and the number of people that the
project will resettle or employ, directly, during construction or operation.

(3) The Authority shall review the project brief and may request the project proponent to amplify
the project brief or to provide any additional information which the Authority may reasonably
require, by a date specified by the Authority.

(4) The Authority may decline the application for an environmental assessment where the
Authority determines that the proposed project site is in an environmentally sensitive area and that
no development may be allowed in that area.

(5) The Authority shall require a new project brief where a project proponent fails to prepare an
initial environmental evaluation, environment impact assessment and comprehensive mitigation plan
within one (1) year of the decision being made.

Categorization of Projects

12. (1) The Authority shall, upon being satisfied that it has sufficient information concerning the
proposed project, within five (5) days from the date of submission of all required information,

 
so

categorize the proposed project as follows, taking into account examples of the types of projects
which would ordinarily be assigned to each category listed in the Second Schedule, -

(a) as a category 1 project where the Authority considers that the proposed project is
unlikely to have any significant adverse environmental impacts:

(b) as a category 2 project where the Authority considers that the proposed project is likely
to have some significant adverse environmental impacts but that the impacts are
relatively well-known and easy to predict and the measures which can be taken to
prevent or mitigate these impacts are well-known; and

(c) as a category 3 project if the Authority considers that the proposed project is likely to
have significant adverse environmental impacts and that in-depth study is required to
determine the scale, extent and significance of the impacts and to identify appropriate
mitigation measures.

(2) In deciding on the categorization of a proposed project the Authority shall take into
consideration all relevant factors including -

(a) nature of the project;

(b) the scale of the proposed project;

(c) its location in relation to environmentally sensitive areas;

(d) any anticipated impacts that the project may have on the environment; and

(e) any relevant policies and legislation pertaining to environment and natural resources
management.

(3) The Minister may by notice in the Gazette, designate areas as environmentally sensitive areas
for purposes of these Regulations in accordance with the Second Schedule.

(4) Subject to sub-regulation (2), the Authority shall, within five (5) days of assigning a proposed
project to a category, prepare a written copy of the decision categorizing the proposed project and the
reasons for the decision.

(5) A decision of the Authority for categorizing of a proposed project prepared in terms of
sub-regulation (5) shall be valid for a period of one (1) year.

Category 1 Projects

13. (1) Where a project is classified under category 1 the Authority shall issue an authorization letter
and shall stipulate the terms and conditions to be complied with by the project proponent.

(2) Where a project cannot not be classified either as category 1 or as category 2, the project
proponent shall be required to prepare an environmental management plan setting out a summary of
the nature of the project, its impacts and the planned mitigation measures to address the environmental
impacts of the project.

Category 2 Projects

14. Where a project is classified under category 2 -

(a) the project proponent shall prepare an initial environment evaluation report and a
comprehensive mitigation plan in accordance with the reporting requirements prescribed

 
Sie

in the Third Schedule and shall within thirty (30) days, submit three (3) hard copies and
an electronic copy of the initial environment evaluation report and the comprehensive
mitigation plan to the Authority together with the fees prescribed in the Eighth Schedule;

(b) the Authority shall, within ten (10) days of receipt of the initial environment evaluation
report and the comprehensive mitigation plan, decide whether the initial environment
evaluation report and the comprehensive mitigation plan conform to the reporting
requirements prescribed in the Third Schedule and to any relevant guidelines published
by the Authority, and —

(i) where the report conforms to the prescribed reporting requirements, the Authority
shall issue an authorization letter;

(ii) where the report does not conform to the prescribed reporting requirements, the
Authority shall order the project proponent to prepare and submit an amended initial
environment report and comprehensive mitigation plan;

(iii) where the documents are accepted, the Authority may order a public review where
it considers that it would be in the interest of the public to carry out a public
review; and

(iv) where the initial environment evaluation and comprehensive mitigation plan have
been referred to public review, the timelines and consultation process specified in
respect of Category 3 projects shall be applicable.

(c) the Authority shall within five (5) days of receipt of the amended documents together with
the prescribed fee, either issue an authorization letter where it considers that the

amended documents comply with the requirements of these Regulations and relevant
guidelines published by the Authority; or notify the project proponent in writing that the
documents have been rejected, giving reasons for that decision; and

(d) where the Authority considers that further studies are necessary to assess the likely impacts
of the project or to identify appropriate mitigation measures, the Authority may by notice,
order the project proponent to prepare and submit an Environmental Impact Assessment
and a revised Comprehensive Mitigation Plan and to follow the procedure laid down in
regulation 14 for projects under category 3.

Category 3 Projects

15. (1) A project proponent in respect of a project classified under category 3 shall, before preparing
an Environmental Impact Assessment report and Comprehensive Mitigation Plan, undertake a
consultation process to involve or include concerned or affected Government agencies, local
authorities, non-governmental organizations and any other interested and affected persons to help
determine the scope and effect of the project or work to be carried out.

(2) Upon complying with sub-regulation (1), the project proponent shall submit a scoping report
to the Authority for determination, including draft terms of reference which shall take into account
the reporting format prescribed in the Third Schedule, the results of the consultation prescribed in
sub-regulation (1) and the environmental impacts and effects listed in the Fourth Schedule.

(3) The Authority shall, within five (5) days after receipt of the scoping report (2) and draft
terms of reference referred to in sub-regulation (1), determine whether or not scoping report (2)
and draft terms of reference are acceptable and where the draft terms of reference are not acceptable,
the Authority shall order the project proponent to prepare and submit acceptable and final terms of
reference.

 
S11

(4) After the Authority has approved the terms of reference, the project proponent shall prepare
an environment impact assessment report and a comprehensive mitigation plan in accordance with
the procedure laid down in the Fifth Schedule and submit three (3) copies of the environment impact
assessment report and the comprehensive mitigation plan to the Authority together with the fee
prescribed in the Eighth Schedule.

(5) The Authority shall within fifteen (15) days of receipt of the environment impact assessment
report and the comprehensive mitigation plan, review the environment impact assessment report
and the comprehensive mitigation plan, and decide whether the environment impact assessment
report and the comprehensive mitigation plan meets the reporting requirements specified in the
Third Schedule and any relevant guidelines published by the Authority.

(6) Where the environment impact assessment and comprehensive mitigation plan reports are

acceptable, the Authority shall issue a notice of acceptance to the project proponent and require the
project proponent to submit eight (8) or more hard copies of the environment impact assessment and
comprehensive mitigation plan as may be determined by the Authority and an electronic copy for
public review.

(7) Where the environment impact assessment and comprehensive mitigation plan reports are
unacceptable, the Authority shall order the project proponent to prepare and submit an amended
environment impact assessment report and comprehensive mitigation plan and notify the project
proponent of the number of copies of the environment impact assessment report and the comprehensive
mitigation plan which the Authority requires for public review.

(8) The Authority shall, within ten (10) days of receipt of the amended documents together with
the prescribed fee either -

(a) issue a notice of acceptance where the Authority considers that the amended
documents comply with the requirements of these Regulations and relevant guidelines
published by the Authority and notify the project proponent to submit a minimum of
eight (8) hard copies and an electronic copy of the environment impact assessment
report and the comprehensive mitigation plan which the Authority requires for public
review purposes; or

(b) Notify the project proponent in writing that the environment impact assessment report
and comprehensive mitigation plan documents have been rejected giving reasons for
the decision.

(9) The Authority shall issue an authorization letter subject to terms and conditions which the
Authority considers appropriate to ensure that the adverse environmental impacts of the project are
satisfactorily mitigated.

(10) The Authority shall not issue an authorization letter, where the Authority considers that the
implementation of the project will cause adverse environmental impacts or that the mitigation
measures may be inadequate to satisfactorily mitigate the environmental impacts of the project;

Strategic environmental assessment

16. (1) Any project proponent who proposes to introduce a Bill, regulation, public policy, programme
or plan that could have an adverse effect on the protection, conservation or enhancement of the
environment or the sustainable management of natural resources shall notify the Authority, prior to
introducing that Bill, regulation, public policy or plan in accordance with the procedure set out in
section 31 of the Act and shall include information prescribed in the Sixth Schedule.

(2) The timelines and consultation process of Category 3 projects shall be applicable to

 
$12
strategic environmental assessments.

(3) Where a project proponent is required to undertake a strategic environmental assessment,
that project proponent shall prepare and submit, to the Authority, terms of reference for carrying
out a strategic environmental assessment of the likely significant and cumulative effects on the
environment of implementing the Bill. regulation, public policy, programme or plan.

(4) Where a strategic environmental assessment has been approved in accordance with this part
the project proponent may be required to submit a project specific environmental assessment which
is linked to the strategic environmental assessment subject to regulation 10.

PART IV
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION, ACCESS TO INFORMATION AND PROTECTION OF
PROPRIETARY INFORMATION

Public Reviews

17. (1) Upon issuing a notice of acceptance in respect of an environment assessment, environment
impact assessment and the accompanying comprehensive mitigation plan, or a summary of any of
these documents, and receipt of any additional copies of these documents from the project proponent,
the Authority shall concurrently -

(a) distribute copies of the documents to concemed and affected Ministries, local authorities,
parastatals, non-governmental organizations and any other person;

(b) display conspicuously such copies in public places or such other places in the vicinity of
the site of the proposed project or existing undertaking; and

(c) the public review in local print and electronic media twice a week for two (2) consecutive
weeks;

specifying the place and the times where copies are available for inspection, inviting objections,
comments or submissions from interested and affected persons, specifying the procedure for the
submission of comments and objections and the date on which the public review period will terminate
in accordance with sub-regulation (2).

(2) The period for public review of the documents referred to in sub-regulation (1) shall be
calculated from the date of the last notification in the newspaper and subject to sub-regulation (3),
the period for public review shall not be less than fifteen (15) days.

(3) The Authority may extend a public review period for a period of not more than five (5) days
where the Authority considers it necessary due to the sensitive nature of a project.

(4) Where the Authority believes a project is likely to have significant impacts on the environment
of a neighboring country or at the request of that neighboring country requests the Authority shall
forward the relevant reports and documents to that country at the same time the reports or documents
are made available for public review in Eswatini.

(5) The Authority shall immediately after receipt of objections, comments or submissions -
(a) acknowledge receipt of all written objections, comments or submissions; and

(b) send a copy of the objections, comments or submissions to the project proponent.
(6) The Authority shall, at the expiration of the public review period specified under sub-

regulations (3) review the comments or submissions and in accordance with regulation 19, and
determine within five (5) days whether or not to hold a public hearing.

 
$13

(7) The Authority shall not disclose or make public the personal information or data of a person
who submitted a written comment or an objection where that person has so requested.

(8) The project proponent shall be responsible for all expenses incurred including expenses
for the preparation of an environment impact assessment, an environment assessment report or a
comprehensive mitigation plan and shall provide sufficient copies during all review procedures.

Public Hearings

18. (1) The Authority shall hold a public hearing, where -
(a) after examining an environment assessment, an environment impact assessment
report or an accompanying comprehensive mitigation plan for a proposed project or
existing undertaking, the Authority is of the opinion that the project or undertaking
is of such a sensitive or significant nature that the public should have the opportunity to
make submissions or comments at a public hearing; or

(b) the public concern over the project is great and the number of written and

substantiated objections are more than exceeds ten (10) in number.
(2) The Authority shall, where a public hearing is to be held -

(a) publish a notice, at least once a week for two (2) consecutive weeks, in a print and
electronic media in Eswatini, stating the date and place where the public hearing is to be
held at least ten (10) days before the public hearing is held and the expenses in respect
of the publication of the notice shall be borne by the project proponent;

(b) display and make available for inspection and photo copying in public or other place
in the vicinity of the proposed project or existing undertaking, all reports, documents,
written comments and objections during and after the period of public review until the
public hearing is finalized; and

(c) call upon any party who has an interest in the outcome of the public hearing,
including the project proponent or project proponent of an existing undertaking, any
government agency and any interested or affected person, to attend the public hearing
or solicit in writing comments from other government agencies or offices with
expertise or regulatory power over the proposed project or existing undertaking.

(3) A public hearing prescribed under sub-regulation (1) shall be held within ten (10) days
after compliance with sub-regulation (2), by the Authority,

(4) Where the Authority is of the opinion that the number and complexity of the issues to be
considered at the hearing requires additional time for preparation by any party to the public
hearing, the Authority may extend the date of the public hearing for a period of ten (10) days.

Appointment of Tribunal
19. (1) The Authority shall appoint a tribunal to conduct public hearings.

(2) The Tribunal shall consist of not less than three (3) and not more than five (5) persons, the
majority of whom shall have the requisite expertise and experience in the issues to be addressed in
the public hearing and one of whom shall be the chairperson.

(3) The period of appointment of members of the Tribunal shall not exceed two (2) months and

shall be guided by the duration of a public hearing which may be determined by the complexity of
the issues to be heard at the.

 
S14
Findings of Public Hearings

20. (1) The Chairperson of the Tribunal shall prepare and deliver a report of the findings of the
Tribunal to the Authority for its determination.

(2) The Authority shall make the report of the findings of the Tribunal public and available for
inspection for a period of not less than fifteen (15) days, and shall advertise details of where and when
it may be inspected and photo copied, in accordance with regulation 20 (1).

Access to Public Documents

21. (1) A project brief, environmental impact assessment report, terms of reference, public comments,
report of the Chairperson of the Tribunal, decision letter or any other information submitted to the
Authority under these Regulations shall be public documents.

(2) The Authority shall, on such terms and conditions as it may determine, grant access to any
person who wishes to access to any of the documents referred to in sub-regulation (1).

Protection of Proprietary Information

22. (1) Where at any stage during the process of implementing these Regulations, the project
proponent claims, in writing, that any information submitted to the Authority is proprietary,
the Authority shall review the claim and may request the project proponent to submit additional
information which it considers necessary to support their claim; and no person shall copy, circulate,
publish or disclose such information until the Authority has made a decision on the claim.
(2) The Authority shall decide within twenty (20) days of a claim made under sub-regulation
(1) whether to treat the information as proprietary or not.

(3) Where the Authority determines that the information referred to in sub-regulation (1) is
proprietary, such information shall be excluded from the project brief, the environmental impact
statement or environmental audit report, and such information shall remain available to the
Authority.

(4) A members of staff of the Authority handling any information which the Authority has
determined to be proprietary, shall not disclose or communicate such information to any unauthorized
person.

(5) Where the Authority rejects a claim that any information is proprietary, the Authority shall
request the project proponent to communicate, in writing, to the Authority, whether the project
proponent intends to -

(a) Waive the claim and continue with the assessment process under these Regulations; or

(b) withdraw the information submitted under these Regulations from the assessment

process.
PART V
AUTHORISATION LETTERS AND ENVIRONMENTAL COMPLIANCE
CERTIFICATES

Issue of authorization letter

23. (1) The Authority shall, within five (5) days after the expiry of the review period or public
review, or if a public hearing has been held, after receipt of a report of a public hearing consider
any environment assessment, initial environment evaluation, environment impact assessment,
environment management plan, comprehensive mitigation plan or summary in respect of which a

 
S15

notice of acceptance has been issued, comments, submissions and objections raised by interested and
affected persons, issue, or refuse to issue, an authorization letter.

(2) The Authority shall issue an authorization letter —

(a) subject to terms and conditions which the Authority considers appropriate to ensure that
the adverse environmental impacts of the undertaking or project are satisfactorily
mitigated; and

(b) where the Authority considers that all the environmental concerns or impacts are ad
equately addressed by the environment assessment, initial environment evaluation,
environment impact assessment or environment management plan report and the
accompanying comprehensive mitigation plan.

(3) The Authority shall not issue an authorization letter in respect of a project, where the
Authority considers that the implementation of the project would bring about unacceptable
environmental impacts or that the mitigation measures may be inadequate to satisfactorily
mitigate the adverse environmental impacts of the proposed project.

Issue of an Environmental Compliance Certificate

24. (1) The Authority shall issue an environmental compliance certificate upon the project
proponent implementing the project activities in accordance with the terms and conditions of the
authorization letter, the comprehensive mitigation plan and upon being satisfied, after considering
project compliance reports, that the project proponent has complied with all the specified terms and
conditions.

(2) The Authority shall issue an environmental compliance certificate in relation to an existing
undertaking upon being satisfied that the conditions specified in the environmental audit and
accompanying comprehensive mitigation plan have been complied with.

(3) The terms and conditions to be complied with by the project proponent of an existing
undertaking, or by the project proponent in a proposed project, shall be specified in the environmental
compliance certificate or authorization letter

(4) The Authority shall not issue an environmental compliance certificate in respect of an existing
undertaking, if the Authority considers that the continued operation of the undertaking is causing,
or is reasonably likely to cause, danger to the environment or the public and that the mitigation
measures proposed in the comprehensive mitigation plan are inadequate to satisfactorily mitigate the
danger and the adverse environmental impacts of the undertaking.

(5) Where the Authority refuses to issue an environmental compliance certificate under
sub-regulation (3), the Authority shall simultaneously give notice to the project proponent to rectify
or remove the cause of danger or potential danger in such manner as the Authority directs.
Communication of Decision by Authority
25. The Authority shall communicate its decision under regulation 24 and 25-

(a) in writing giving reasons for its decision;

(b) by publishing that decision in a medium to be decided by the Authority;

(c) by publishing a detailed statement of the decision for public inspection in the manner
prescribed in regulation 20(1); and

 
S16

(d) by sending a copy of the decision to any person who has, in writing, submitted
comments or lodged an objection to the Authority in terms of these Regulations.

Project Implementation and Monitoring

26. (1) A person to whom an authorization letter or an environmental compliance certificate is
issued shall be responsible for implementing the comprehensive mitigation plan which forms part of
the authorization letter or environmental compliance certificate, and for monitoring the environmental
impacts of the project or existing undertaking and the implementation of the comprehensive
mitigation plan.

(2) The project proponent of an existing undertaking shall commence implementation of the
comprehensive mitigation plan immediately after the date of issue of the environmental compliance
certificate and the Authority shall monitor the undertaking to ensure that the project proponent is
complying with the comprehensive mitigation plan.

(3) The holder of an authorization letter or environmental compliance certificate shall
submit periodic project compliance reports containing information on the implementation of the
comprehensive mitigation plan and compliance with the directions of the Authority.

(4) Any person who monitors the implementation of a project or a comprehensive mitigation
plan and who discovers that any term or condition of the environmental compliance certificate is not
being complied with, or that unforeseen damage to the environment is occurring, shall immediately
report this to the Authority.

Expiry and renewal of authorization letter

27. (1) An authorization letter shall expire after a period of three (3) years from the date of issue if
by that date, no substantial progress has been made in implementing the project such as earthworks
or construction work, or if the project has been abandoned or postponed.

(2) Where an authorization letter has expired and the project proponent intends to revive and
proceed with the project, that project proponent shall submit a revised project brief to the Authority.

(3) Where the project proponent intends to proceed in terms of sub-regulation (2), the project
proponent shall inform the Authority of any changes or differences in the revised project brief and
the project brief sanctioned in the expired authorization letter.

(4) Upon receipt of the revised project brief the Authority shall determine -

(a) whether the project proponent ought to prepare an additional initial environment
assessment or environment impact assessment report, and a comprehensive mitigation
plan; or

(b) whether the project proponent ought to do additional work to supplement an initial
environment evaluation, environment impact assessment report, or comprehensive
mitigation plan.

(5) Where the Authority determines that an additional initial environment evaluation,
environment impact assessment report or accompanying comprehensive mitigation plan should be
done, the provisions of regulation 13 or 14, including the payment of the prescribed fees prescribed
shall apply to that project.

(6) Where the Authority determines that only supplementary work to the existing initial
environment evaluation report, environment impact assessment report, and comprehensive mitigation
plan is required, the Authority shall advise the project proponent as to the nature of the additional

 
S17

work or information that is required and the project proponent shall undertake the additional work
and provide the required information before proceeding with the project.

(7) The Authority shall, on receipt of the additional work or required information, make
additional work or required information open for public review by displaying or distributing the
work or information for review by any interested or affected person.

(8) An interested or affected person may, within ten (10) days from the first day of the review,

submit their objections or comments to the Authority

(9) The Authority shall within five (5) days after the expiry of the period for submission of
objections and comments, decide in accordance with this regulation whether or not to issue an
authorization letter in respect of the project.

Expiry and Renewal of Environmental Compliance Certificate

28. (1) An environmental compliance certificate issued in accordance with this Part shall expire after
a period of two (2) years from the date of its issue and shall be renewable for such further periods
as the Authority shall determine, taking into account the nature of the project and its impacts on the
environment and the effectiveness of the implementation of the mitigation measures stated in the
comprehensive mitigation plan.

(2) An application for renewal of an environmental compliance certificate shall be accompanied
by a form prescribed by the Authority together with the prescribed project implementation reports
and fees.

(3) The Authority shall renew an environmental compliance certificate if upon considering the
project implementation reports and upon inspecting the project the Authority determines that the
terms and conditions of the comprehensive mitigation plan have been complied with.

(4) Where upon inspection of the undertaking and review of the project implementation reports
the Authority determines that the terms and conditions of the comprehensive mitigation plan have not
been complied with, the Authority shall order that an environmental audit be conducted in accordance
with Regulation 16.

Suspension, Amendment and Cancellation of authorization letters and Environmental
Compliance Certificates

29. (1) Where, on the basis of information which has become available to the Authority after the
issue of an authorization letter or an environmental compliance certificate, the Authority considers
that the implementation of the project or the continued operation of the undertaking is causing, or is
reasonably likely to cause, danger to the environment or to the public, the Authority may-

(a) suspend the environmental compliance certificate and give notice to the project
proponent to rectify or remove the cause of danger or potential danger in accordance
with such directions to be prescribed by the Authority;

(b) give the project proponent a reasonable opportunity of proposing amendments to the
environmental compliance certificate which are acceptable to the Authority; or

(c) subject to sub-regulation (2), amend or cancel the environmental compliance certificate
by notice in writing to the project proponent.

(2) The Authority shall not cancel an environmental compliance certificate unless the Authority
is of the view that the danger to, or adverse effect on the environment or the public cannot be
satisfactorily mitigated.

Offences and penalties

commits an offence and shall on conviction be liable to a fine not exceeding one hundred thousand

(b) compensate any person, including the Authority, who has or is likely to, suffer loss or

(c) cancellation of an authorization letter, license or permit; or

(d) suspension of an authorization or decision letter, license or permit subject to whatever terms

GUIDELINES FOR DESIGNATION OF ENVIRONMENTALLY SENSITIVE AREAS

1, The designation of an area as environmentally sensitive shall meet one or more of the following
three (3) categories of general objectives —

(a) conservation of natural resources and protection of the environment;
(b) sustainable human and economic development; and
(c) logistic support such as environmental education and information sharing.

2. The designation of an area as environmentally sensitive shall meet one (1) or more of the
following specific objectives -

(a) appreciation of the broader ecological aspects of an area for its intrinsic values and

functions as well as its potential for direct material benefits;
(b) maintenance of the significance of an area in the national, regional and international context;
(c) preservation of the biological diversity of the area;

(d) preservation of the integrity of an area and its attributes with the aim of sustaining its
potential for direct material benefits;

(e) maintenance of the role of the area in the functioning of the wider ecosystem;

(f) protection, preservation, management or rehabilitation of an area that is fragile, threatened
or degraded;

(g) regulation of the use of natural resources contained within the area;

(h) maintenance of the cultural values of an area which are associated with preserving the
integrity of the environment;

 
$22
(i) maintenance of stock of genetic resources in viable populations;
(f) facilitation of relevant scientific research or environmental monitoring to improve under
standing of interactions between biotic and abiotic components of the environment, the
Processes involved and the attributes and potential of the resources of area; and

g) dissemination of information to stakeholders and the public at large.

3. The designation of an area as environmentally sensitive shall be on the basis of one or more of
the following general or specific criteria -

General criteria:
(a) uniqueness, rarity or importance of biological features;
(b) good representation of naturally-occurring ecological system or type;

(c) particularly good representation of an ecosystem of one, or common to more than one
biogeographical region;

(d) critical to the survival or recovery of endangered, endemic or vulnerable
species/communities of plants or animals;

(e) rare or unusual habitat, ecosystem, or community attributes in a biograghical area;
(f) an appreciable or significant assemblage of endangered species of plants or animals;
(g) special value as a habitat for plants and animals at a critical stage of their biological cycle;

(h) provision of appreciable social recreation or economic benefit to local communities or
wider areas;

(i) forest, purely conservation purposes;
(j) unique geological features;
(k) high in aesthetic value;

(1) Regarded by the scientific community as having significant value for non-destructive
research;

(m) Potential for fostering environmental awareness, appreciation or education;

(n) Performing an integral role in the functioning of the wider ecosystem; and

(0) Representative example of all wetland types.

Specific criteria:
(a) strict nature reserve: an area requiring protection for science that possesses some
outstanding or representative ecosystems, geological or physiological features or species,
available primarily for scientific research or environmental monitoring;

(b) national Park: an area requiring —

 
$23

(i) the protection of the ecological integrity of one or more ecosystems for present and
future generations;

(ii) the exclusion of exploitation occupation inimical to the purposes of designation of the
area, and

(iii) the provision of a spiritual, scientific, educational, recreational and visitor
opportunities, all of which are culturally and environmentally compatible;

(c) natural Monument: an area containing one or more specific natural or cultural features of
outstanding or unique value that require conservation because of inherent rarity,
representative or aesthetic qualities or cultural significance;

(d) Habitat or species management area: an area requiring conservation through management

intervention to ensure the maintenance of habitats or to meet the requirements of specific

species;

protected landscape: an area that may require protection for conservation and recreation,
where the interaction of people and nature over time has produced an area of distinct
character, with significant aesthetic, ecological or cultural value, and often with high
biological value; and

(e

(d) managed resource protected area: an area containing predominately unmodified natural
systems that require sustainable use and management to ensure long-term maintenance and
protection of biological diversity, while providing at the same time a sustainable flow of
natural products and services to meet community needs.

GUIDELINES FOR PROJECT PROPONENTS IN CONDUCTING ENVIRONMENTAL
IMPACT ASSESSMENT

STAGE 1: PRELIMINARY ACTIONS.

(a) The description of the Project as in the Project Brief Submitted to the Authority.

(b) The project proponent appoints a coordinator who is a qualified Environmental Assessment
Practitioner for the environmental impact study. The qualification of the coordinator
depend on the nature of the project.

(c) Together with the coordinator, the project proponent selects the experts that will comprise
the team that will undertake the study. Preference should be given to experts with specific
knowledge of local or similar conditions. The team shall include at least one person

resident in the potentially affected area.

(d) The coordinator allocates work to the team member of the purpose of carrying out the
scoping exercise.

(e) The team reviews and determines the applicable laws, regulations and standards.

(f) The project proponent, the coordinator and the team identify the various alternatives for the

 
$29
development of the project (sites, technology and design).
STAGE 2: SCOPING (OR IDENTIFICATION OF IMPACTS)

(1) The team under the guidance of the coordinator identifies all the possible environmental
impacts of the project.

(2) The coordinator, the team and the Authority determines which of the impacts shall be the
subject of the study based on the following criteria -

(a) magnitude, including the impact of the project on environmental resources;
(b) extent, including the geographical extent of the impact;

(c) significance, including the actual effects of the impacts on the environmental resource;
and

(d) special sensitivity, including impacts which are significant in the specific local
economic, social and ecological setting.

(e) impact of climate change; and
(f) proneness to disasters and environmental hazards.

(3) The project proponent submits the names and qualifications of all persons to carry out the
study to the Authority for approval.

STAGE 3: BASELINE STUDY

The team undertakes a detailed description of the existing environment including the social an eco-
nomic activities of the population resident in the potentially affected area.

STAGE 4: IMPACT EVALUATION

The team predicts and evaluates the various predicted impacts and ranks them in order of importance
on the basis of two criteria:

(1) Quantitative change where change can be quantified.

(2) Quantitative change where change cannot be quantified, but instead the impact of the
project depends on the environmental acceptability of the project.

STAGE 5: PUBLIC PARTICIPATION IN ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT STUDY
(1) The team seeks the view of the community which are likely to be affected by the project.
(2) The views sought in (1) are considered in the development of mitigation measures.

STAGE 6: IDENTIFICATION OF MITIGATION MEASURES

(1) The team identifies measures for elimination (where possible), or reduction, of
environmental impacts for various alternatives identified in the study such as -

(a) engineering works in noise reduction, prior treatment of effluent air pollution
reduction measures and solid waste minimization through reclamation, recycling and
any other appropriate measures; and

 
$30

(b) management measures especially in areas of natural resources, reforestation, control of
soil erosion, desalinization, desilting.

(2) The team includes the cost mitigation measures into impact evaluation.
(3) Where necessary, the team will create an alternative based on the mitigation.
STAGE 7: ASSESSMENT (OR COMPARISON OF ALTERNATIVES)

(1) The team compares all the alternatives from the basis of economic, socio-cultural and
environmental gains and costs.

(2) The team ranks and recommends all alternatives to the project proponent on the basis of
sound environmental and economic analysis.

STAGE 8: DECISION MAKING

The project proponent makes a decision choosing one alternative and giving reasons for the rejecting
the other alternatives.

STAGE 9: SUBMISSION OF THE REPORT TO THE AUTHORITY
(1) The team completes the environmental impact statement; and
(2) The project proponent submits the report to the Authority.
STAGE 10: IMPLEMENTATION OF THE PROJECT AND POST ASSESSMENT AUDITS

(1) If the Authority approves the environmental impact statement the project proponent may
implement the project.

(2) The team shall carry out a post assessment environmental audit between 12-36 months of the
commencement of the project in accordance with these Regulations.

SIXTH SCHEDULE
(Under regulation 16)

CRITERIA FOR DETERMINING WHETHER A BILL, REGULATION, POLICY OR
PLAN REQUIRES A STRATEGIC ENVIRONMENTAL ASSESSMENT

The Characteristic of the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme, in particular, having regard to -
(a) the degree to which the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme sets the framework for
projects and other activities, either with regard to the location, nature, size and operating

conditions or allocating resources;

(b) the degree to which the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme influences other Bills,
regulations, policies, plans or programmes;

(c) the probability, frequency, duration and reversibility of the effects;
(d) the transboundary nature of the effects:

(e) the cumulative nature of the effects;

 
S31

(f) the risks to human health and the environment, such as due to accidents;
(g) the magnitude and spatial extent of the effects of the impacts;
(h) the geographical area and population to be affected;
(i) the value and vulnerability of the area to be affected due to -

(i) special characteristics or cultural heritage;

(ii) exceeded environmental quality standards or limit values; and

(iii) intensive land use; and

(j)_ the effects on area and landscapes which have a recognized national, regional or
international protection status.

SEVENTH SCHEDULE
(Under regulation 16)

INFORMATION TO BE INCLUDED IN A STRATEGIC ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT
STATEMENT

The following issues shall be addressed in a strategic environmental assessment report —
(a) an outline of contents and main objectives of then Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme;

(b) relevant aspects of the current state of the environment and the likely evolution thereof
without implementation of the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme;

(c) the environmental characteristics of areas likely to be affected by the Bill, regulation,
policy, plan or programme;

(d) environmental protection objectives, established at international, regional or national level,
which are relevant to the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme and the way those
objectives and any environmental considerations have been taken into account during its
preparation;

(e) the likely significant effects on the environment, including on issues such as biodiversity,
population, human health, fauna, flora, soil, water, air, climate factors, material assets,
cultural heritage including architectural and archaeological heritage, landscape and the
interrelationship between the above factors;

(f) the measures envisaged to reduce, prevent and as fully as possible offset any significant
adverse effects on the environment of implementing the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or
programme;

(g) an outline of the reasons for selecting the alternatives dealt with and a description of how
the assessment was undertaken including any difficulties (such as technical deficiencies or
lack of know-how) encountered in compiling the required information;

(h) a description of the measures envisaged concerning monitoring of the significant
environmental effects of implementing the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme; and

 
$32

(i) anon-technical summary of the information provided under paragraphs (a) — (h).

EIGHTH SCHEDULE
FEES
(Under regulation 32)

(a) The fees to be charged for category 1 projects shall be 0.001 of the development cost of the
Project.

(b) The fees to be charged for EMP and category 2 projects shall be 0.002 of the development
cost of the Project.

(c) The fees to be charged for category 3 projects shall be 0.003 of the development cost of the
Project.

(d) The fees charged for strategic environmental assessment shall be 0.003 of the development
cost of the Bill, regulation, policy, plan or programme.

(e) The fees charged for auditing existing projects and renewal of an environmental
compliance certificate shall be 0.001 of the development cost of the project.

(f) The fees charged for resubmission of any document required under these Regulations shall
be 50% of the initial fees.

g) The fees for registration of Environmental Assessment Practitioners shall be Three
Thousand Emalangeni (E3000.00).

(h) The fees for renewal of registration shall be Five Hundred Emalangeni (E500.00)
per annum
